cards.b: A named block of code that does a specific job and can be called from elsewhere in the program.
A function returns a value to the caller (RETURN); a procedure does not.
Code is reused, program is shorter, easier to read, test and debug, and work can be shared.
A variable named in the subprogram definition that receives the value passed in when it is called.
Local: declared in a subprogram and only usable there. Global: declared outside and usable anywhere.
An automated check that data entered is reasonable and acceptable for the program to process.
Tests that a value lies between limits, e.g. a mark from 0 to 100.
Length: number of characters. Presence: not left empty. Format: matches a pattern, e.g. email has @.
Tests that the data is the right type, e.g. an age is a whole number.
Code breaks the rules of the language, so the program will not run, e.g. a missing bracket.
The program starts but crashes while running, e.g. dividing by zero or index out of range.
The program runs but gives wrong results, e.g. a + b / 2 instead of (a + b) / 2.
Valid, typical data that should be accepted.
Data at the very edge of the valid range, just inside and just outside, e.g. 0, 100, -1, 101.
Invalid or wrong-type data that should be rejected, e.g. text where a number is needed.

gaps.s: A subprogram that returns a value is a ___.
A variable declared inside a subprogram is a ___ variable.
A check that a value lies between two limits is a ___ check.
An error that crashes the program while it is running is a ___ error.
A typing mistake that breaks the language rules is a ___ error.
A test plan lists the test data, its type and the ___ outcome.
Data just inside or outside the limit of valid data is called ___ data.
A value passed into a subprogram when it is called is an ___.

short.q: Give two benefits of using subprograms.
short.model: They let you reuse code instead of repeating it, and each small part is easier to read, test and debug.
points: easier to test/debug/read or share work

short.q: A quantity must be from 1 to 50. Give one normal, two boundary and one erroneous test value with expected results.
short.model: Normal: 20 accepted. Boundary: 1 and 50 accepted (or 0 and 51 rejected). Erroneous: 'abc' rejected with an error message.

short.q: Name the type of error for each: (a) a missing bracket, (b) dividing by zero while running, (c) adding VAT using the wrong percentage.
short.model: (a) syntax error, (b) runtime error, (c) logic error.
points: runtime for divide by zero and logic for wrong percentage

short.q: Write a Python function double(n) that returns twice n, and show it being called.
short.model: def double(n): return n * 2, then print(double(4)) which outputs 8.

short.q: Describe how a validation loop for a password of at least 8 characters would work.
short.model: Ask for the password, check its length, and if it is less than 8 characters show an error message and ask again. Repeat until it is 8 or more, then accept it.
points: repeats with error message until valid
